text:
julia_acmecorp: Hey team, we're seeing a bunch of 500/timeout errors and 600-900ms p99 latency from our users in EU while they hit our Redwood-hosted endpoint. Started ~10:20 UTC. Request IDs: r-0a1b2c3d4e and r-0f9e8d7c6b. Any known incidents?
sara_support: sorry you're hit, can you confirm the region you're configured for? EU users should be routed to eu-west1 by our routing policy.
julia_acmecorp: Our tenant config is `region_preference: EU` and we've pinned `gpt-medium-v2` in eu-west1. We see logs showing requests forwarded to `us-east1` sometimes. Here's a trace from a customer session: `trace: s->edge-proxy->smart-router->us-east1:inference`
mike_infra: can you paste the raw trace/span IDs? need to check routegen heuristics.
julia_acmecorp: pasted (redacted):
```
POST /v1/generate 200ms
trace_id=312fa3
span: client->edge-proxy (eu-west1)
span: edge-proxy->routegen (eu-west1)
span: routegen->smart-router (us-west2)
span: smart-router->inference-host (us-east1)
```
sara_support: interesting — routegen chose `us-west2` then smart-router forwarded to `us-east1`. That explains cross-region hop. Not a simple DNS issue.
alex_sre: can we get the routing policy for that tenant? maybe fallback rules or capacity fallback triggered?
mike_infra: fetching tenant policy from the control plane now. I see `preferred_region: eu-west1`, `fallback_order: [eu-west1, us-west2, us-east1]`, `capacity_threshold: 0.65`. At the time of the trace, eu-west1 latency SLO was okay but available GPU slots were at 100% (per dedicated pool metrics). The router may have applied failover.
julia_acmecorp: but why routegen picked us-west2 instead of the configured next EU region? we only have eu-west1 for EU.
mike_infra: good question — routegen has a region grouping rule that sometimes picks the least-cost region matching latency/cost score. If eu-west1 is saturated and the next in fallback is a region in the same geo group, it would pick that; but here it picked us-west2 which is in a different geo group.
sara_support: could be a bug where the geo group calculation for tenant-level policies is omitted when `dedicated` flag is true. Are you using Dedicated capacity?
julia_acmecorp: yes, we have Dedicated with a small committed pool.
alex_sre: I want to reproduce. Sara, can you run a synthetic that simulates high saturation on eu-west1 and then hit routegen for that tenant? Use these curl headers: `X-Tenant: acme-corp`, `X-Request-Id: repro-1`
sara_support: running now. Probe script:
```
for i in 1..200 do
  curl -s -H "X-Tenant: acme-corp" -H "X-Request-Id: repro-$i" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
done
```
(sending)
mike_infra: got traces from the probe, I'm seeing the same pattern: routegen returns candidate `us-west2` and smart-router picks `us-east1`. That second hop is odd.
alex_sre: paste a sample trace from the repro with spans and decision metadata.
mike_infra: sample:
```
trace_id=9b7c2a
routegen.decisions: {candidates: [eu-west1(us-availability=0.0), us-west2(latency_score=0.65), us-east1(latency_score=0.6)], reason: capacity_saturated}
smart-router.forward: {target: us-east1, up_metric: 0.98}
```
julia_acmecorp: so routegen picked us-west2 but smart-router chose us-east1? sounds like mismatch between components.
sara_support: that matches a hypothesis: there's an async cache in smart-router that can return a different view of region health due to stale updates. If routegen consults control-plane snapshot and smart-router consults long-term health cache, they could diverge.
alex_sre: right — we recently gated cache TTL changes to reduce control-plane load. Could be regressions causing stale region scores. Rolling back that TTL change might help.
mike_infra: raising an action: rollback region-score-ttl for smart-router to 15s from 5m. Patching now.
deploy-bot: deploy initiated: smart-router config rollback (change-id cfg-2026-03-17-ttlrback).
sara_support: meanwhile, for your tenant, I'll add a temporary per-tenant `strict_geo_enforce: true` to force routegen to only pick eu-west1 or failover to nearest EU clusters (if available). That will prevent US detours while we fix cache.
julia_acmecorp: appreciated — will that cause errors if eu-west1 is fully saturated? we need requests to succeed even if slower.
alex_sre: with `strict_geo_enforce` the router will not pick distant regions but will allow queued requests or queued fallback; we have a queued overflow path. If that's unacceptable, we can enable cross-geo but pin to `us-west2` only. Which do you prefer?
julia_acmecorp: prefer queued over crossing to US for compliance reasons. Please queue.
mike_infra: smart-router rollback applied; I can already see region-score updates propagating. New traces show routegen->smart-router both agree on `us-west2` as next candidate, but with strict_geo enforced the chosen action is to queue.
sara_support: setting tenant flag now. Done.
julia_acmecorp: testing now from EU clients.
(5m later)
julia_acmecorp: latency p99 back down to ~180ms, no more cross-Atlantic hops. Errors dropped to near zero. Thanks.
alex_sre: root cause summary for postmortem draft: config change increased region-score TTL in smart-router from 15s to 5m, leading to stale health view vs control plane. Under saturation, routegen chose fallback candidate list and smart-router used stale scores to forward to a non-preferred far region, creating cross-region hop and p99 spike.
sara_support: actions: 1) revert TTL (done), 2) add integration test that compares routegen and smart-router candidate lists on config change, 3) add tenant-level strict_geo_enforce flag docs, 4) alert when cross-geo hop detected for tenants with `region_preference` set.
julia_acmecorp: please add contact for support escalation if we see this again.
sara_support: noted, assigning `oncall:alex_sre` as escalation.
alex_sre: I'll own the follow-up postmortem and the integration test. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
sara_support: closing the thread once the postmortem is up.
